differences.openwhisper: Settings > API & MCP shows 'Live events and automation' under the MCP cards: the Live API card (permissions, address, endpoints, curl), MCP Events (subscribe switch, count, Clear) and the Claude Code channel card.
differences.fiorivoce: The running app's MCP control is the local session (session_mcp.cpp, session_only() true), and McpSettingsView hides LiveAutomationSection over it; the section and its cards exist and are tested against a full listener (test_live_section.cpp, test_mcp_extras.cpp).
differences.reason: The local MCP session serves saved content only: the live API is never mounted and no McpEvents is built, so the cards would offer switches that do nothing.

differences.openwhisper: When a host is paired, Settings > API & MCP shows a segmented 'This computer / <host>' bar (details 'MCP on/off', 'Host · not allowed', 'Host · needs update', 'Host · unreachable', 'Host · checking…'); the host tab is a second McpSettingsPage over HostMcpSettings/HostMcpServer/HostMcpLink that polls the host every 500 ms and changes its MCP settings, with a gate card ('<host> hasn't allowed this yet', '<host> needs an update', 'Can't reach <host>') and Check again, a note that the live cards are per computer, and it opens on the host tab when only the host's MCP runs.
differences.fiorivoce: McpSettingsView::bindRemote adds a 'Paired computer: <host>' frame (mcpPairedHost) below this computer's page, shown only while paired: 'Check host MCP status' reads the granted session's state once per click, 'Start the authorized host session…' asks first and sends only {enabled: true} for the fixed loopback session, 'End host session' disconnects (the host then revokes the grant). Refusals read '<host> hasn't allowed this yet.' (naming the host's grant), '<host> needs an update.' and 'Can't reach <host>.' in the frame's status line. There are no tabs, host page, gate card or note: this computer's page and cards never hide.
differences.reason: A peer may not change the host's MCP configuration; it only starts and ends the read-only 15-minute session the host granted it, whose token stays on the host, so there is no host page to manage and nothing to poll.

differences.openwhisper: API & MCP has a 'Share this computer's history through the paired host's MCP' tile (mcpShareHistoryTile, disabled with ' Pair a host in Remote engine to enable this setting.' when unpaired) that persists remote_client_history through service.set_share_history, plus the gate bodies naming 'Allow paired computers to manage MCP', the per-computer host note and the tabs' 'Whose MCP to manage' name.
differences.fiorivoce: There is no persistent history-sharing consent: history is shared only in a session opened from Remote engine's 'Share history for this session…' (remote_history::Publication, at most 15 minutes, ended by closing it or disconnecting), which Settings search finds for 'share history'. RemoteEngineControl::set_share_history, which nothing called, was removed. The gate bodies and note belong to the replaced host tab (a21-paired-host-frame).
differences.reason: A named peer views this computer's latest dictations and meeting metadata only during an explicitly opened, time-limited session; a standing opt-in would expose history for as long as the pairing lasts.

differences.openwhisper: Route by voice's status line is computed at once on the GUI thread, including the parts that depend on the judge's API key.
differences.fiorivoce: The status that needs no key (Route by voice off, for example) shows at once; a status that depends on the key is worked out on the io executor, and until that answer arrives the line is empty and the privacy caption shows.
differences.reason: Reading the credential store must not block the GUI thread.
differences.source: The lead's decision of 2026-11-19 on open item ui_automation (M5.13); src/ui_automation/actions_page.cpp requestStatus and automation::status_without_key (src/automation/routing.h); tests/ui_automation/test_sweep_relay_status.cpp ('the route by voice status that needs no key shows before the full answer')
